stories.title: Syria, Israel hold US-mediated talks in Jordan to de-escalate tensions
stories.summary: Syria’s foreign minister meets with an Israeli delegation led by the chief of the Mossad to de-escalate tensions after an Israeli strike near the Turkish border. Syria’s Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani has met with Israeli intelligence officials in Jordan, according to Syrian state media, as the two sides work to de-escalate tensions following an Israeli attack on a Syrian airbase near the Turkish border. Syria’s Sana news agency, citing a diplomatic source, said the talks were mediated by the United States and involved a “high-level Israeli delegation”. The AFP news agency reported that al-Shaibani met the head of Israel’s Mossad intelligence agency, Roman Gofman. According to Sana, the discussions “focused on establishing practical mechanisms to halt Israeli attacks, arrests and targeting operations” as well as “reviving negotiations for a lasting security agreement between the two sides”. They also discussed efforts to ease tensions between Israel and Turkiye and to prevent their rivalry from spilling onto Syrian territory, Sana reported. The US has sought to broker a security agreement between Israel and the government of Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa for more than a year. Israel has launched hundreds of strikes on Syria since the fall of longtime ruler Bashar al-Assad in December 2024 and sent troops into a United Nations-patrolled buffer zone that had long separated Israeli and Syrian forces in the Israeli-occupied Golan Heights. It also bombed the Abu Duhur airbase in northwestern Idlib on Thursday, claiming the attack was to prevent Turkish troops from deploying at the base, a claim Syria and Turkiye have denied. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan have also traded barbs since the incident, with tensions high between the two leaders. According to Sana, the Syrian side stressed during Sunday’s talks “that Syria is a sovereign state with the full right to rebuild and develop its national army and determine its alliances and partnerships in line with its national interests”. The Syrian side rejected “any arrangements or mechanisms that would restrict these sovereign rights,” it said.

stories.title: Haze triggers surge of asthma cases in Malaysia
stories.summary: Upper respiratory tract infection cases also increased, rising by 124 per cent.
article_sentences: Asthma cases in Malaysia surged by 259% due to haze, with unhealthy air quality recorded in seven areas, prompting health warnings to limit outdoor activities.
Heat-related illnesses increased, especially among Malaysia Games participants, but the situation remains under control and is closely monitored.
The Kuala Selangor Wellness Hub supports weight management and mental health, aiming to help an ageing population age with dignity and stay productive.
KUALA SELANGOR, Selangor – Asthma cases rose by 259 per cent in the latest epidemiological week amid haze affecting several parts of Malaysia, said Health Minister Dzulkefly Ahmad.
He said the number of asthma cases detected through the Health Ministry’s sentinel surveillance system increased from 61 in epidemiological week 32 to 219 in week 33.
Upper respiratory tract infection cases rose by 124 per cent, from 1,637 to 3,674 during the same period.
Conjunctivitis cases, however, fell by 7 per cent, from 157 to 146.
Dzulkefly said seven areas recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as at 8am on Aug 23.
Serian in Sarawak recorded the highest reading at 197, followed by Kuching at 185, Sri Aman at 178, Samarahan at 176 and Sarikei at 128.
Sungai Petani in Kedah and Taiping in Perak both recorded readings of 126.
An API reading of 101 to 200 is classified as unhealthy.
A reading of 201 to 300 is very unhealthy, while readings above 300 are hazardous.
